study_scope: three-node LR-WPAN link calibration; not an implementation or ranking of network controllers
fragment_mapping: five 100-byte data fragments each carrying a 4-byte application fragmentation identifier, 104-byte MAC payload per frame; receiver counts a message complete only when all five distinct fragments arrive
pan_and_phy: 2.4 GHz, one PAN, short addresses, ACK enabled, range propagation 120 m; rate from ns-3 LR-WPAN 250 kbps; no 6LoWPAN
mac: unslotted CSMA-CA, max frame retries 3, min BE 3, max BE 5, max CSMA backoffs 4

scenarios.single: one sender at -100 m, starts at 1 s
scenarios.serial: two hidden senders at -100/+100 m, starts at 1.0 s and 1.1 s
scenarios.contending: two mutually audible senders at -50/+50 m, both start at 1.0 s
scenarios.hidden: two mutually hidden senders at -100/+100 m, both start at 1.0 s

rng: ns-3 global seed 1, independent run numbers 1..128, streams assigned beginning 100
endpoints: sender-level fragment-success and five-distinct-fragment message completion
elapsed time from five MAC requests to last confirmation and last unique reception
PHY transmit attempts/bytes (ACKs counted separately by device), PHY receive drops
illustrative transceiver energy from ns-3 state durations and CC2420 typical 3.3 V currents

energy_assumptions.state_mapping: TX_ON and BUSY_TX use TX current; RX_ON and BUSY_RX use RX current; remaining/transitional states use 0 in this illustrative estimate
energy_assumptions.caveat: This is not hardware measurement and excludes CPU, sensing, voltage conversion and any omitted state consumption; TX_ON is an approximate state mapping.

guard_interpretation: The 20 ms Guard is an abstract charged transaction opportunity and is not claimed to contain a complete 500-byte packet, ACKs, backoffs, or retransmissions.
reporting: Report all four scenarios and all outcomes, including unsuccessful fragments and indefinite timing where no full message completes.
